title: Costs rebuild 2 · piece 4: the cost read sums request records (records-first cutover)
description:
**Piece 4 of LIN-4195** (Harbour). It covers D6, D7 and D13. This is the piece that changes figures.

**Fold (D6):**

* Add `foldRequestUsage(records)`: pure, in `lib/row-usage.js` or a sibling. It returns the `foldLineageUsage` shape (`completeness`, `tokens`, `costUsd`, `unpricedModels`, `last`) plus per-model costs.
* Each record is priced with piece 1's per-request pricing; native `costUsd` wins when present.
* Completeness:
  * `complete` when every record is priced;
  * `unpriced` when any record is not, and the figure is withheld (the LIN-4176 rule);
  * `no-usage` when there are no records and no snapshot.
* Labels:
  * `model` is the model with the largest priced cost (ties: latest);
  * `effort` and `harness` are the latest record's.
* **Review note 3:** `incomplete` / `missingCanChangeFigure` is false for a record lineage, because records are fetched by anchor regardless of which rows the caller loaded. State this in code and test it.

**Cutover (D7):** decided in one function in `lib/cost-read.js`.

* A lineage with any request record reads from records only.
* A lineage with none reads snapshots exactly as today.
* **Review note 9:** scope the cutover per harness (snapshots of harness H are ignored when the lineage has records of harness H), or keep piece 0's control asserting that no lineage mixes harnesses. Pick one and say which. Per-harness scoping is one line and covers the window before piece 5.

**Readers (D13, broadened by review notes 1–2):**

* `readCost`, `lineageRecords` and `lineageFigureOf` take a **required** `requestRows` argument and throw on `undefined`.
* The one loader is `RequestUsageStore.listForAnchors`. Pass its result from every caller:
  * `routes/proxy-compute.js` (`/cost`);
  * `lib/model-routing-spend.js` via `lib/model-routing-history.js`;
  * `lib/effort-readout.js`;
  * `lib/kpi-stats.js` and `lib/terminal-marked-task-cost.js` (`/kpis`);
  * `lib/workspace-kpi-stats.js`, which also feeds `lib/weekly-budget.js`;
  * `lib/run-view.js`.
* **Review note 1:** `harnessReadingOf` in `lib/terminal-marked-task-cost.js:99-104` reads snapshots via `usageStateOf(...).usage` and `isRunningTotal` to produce `opencodeSummedShare`/`unknownHarnessShare` (published by `lib/render-kpis.js`).
  * For a record lineage, derive its harness from its records.
  * Count a record lineage as "not delta-summed".
* Broaden the census beyond the read's callers to every reader of snapshot usage outside the legacy fold: `usageStateOf`, `usageOf`/`lastUsageEntry` (`lib/dispatch-lineage.js`), `readRowUsage`/`readUsageEntry`, and `isRunningTotal`. Model it on `tests/unit/cost-read-census.test.js`.
  * `lib/digest-feedback.js` `kpiUsageEntry` and `lib/kpi-stats.js:460` may stay, because they only feed the legacy fold.
* Confirm whether `lib/session-telemetry.js` `buildSessionTelemetry` has a reader. Delete it or leave it, and say which.
* **Volume:** use a plain projection fetch, unless piece 3 measured it as too slow. In that case build the D13 pre-sum fallback; the record shape stays the same.

**Replay change list:** this is the exact diff against piece 0's baseline goldens. Anything else that differs is a defect.

* (a) Haiku over 100k: null → priced on S1, S5, S6, S8, S9, S10, S11, S12, S13.
* (b) Mixed-model: priced per model, and the label becomes the cost-dominant model.
* (c) Subagent lineage: cost rises by the subagent share.
* (d) `<synthetic>` tail: null → priced.
* (e) One-turn, killed or reaped: no-telemetry → priced.
* (f) Resumed across the deploy: equals the oracle and is counted once.
* **Review note 1:** the `opencodeSummedShare`/`unknownHarnessShare` movement goes on the list, or is asserted as a control.
* Controls, asserted unchanged:
  * a single-model, tier-free, subagent-free session (to 1e-9);
  * snapshot-only lineages;
  * S2, S3, S4 and S7.

**Mutation check:** reading snapshots when records exist makes case (f) double count, and the test fails.

**Report:**

* **Review note 10:** name the label change in (b) in the PR and on LIN-4195. It moves lineages between groups on Models and the effort read-out, which is John's call.
* Report the live priced share after deploy, per piece 3's method.

**Acceptance:**

* The replay diff equals the change list exactly, with each listed item seen to differ.
* The census and the required-argument throw are in place.
* All suites are green.

---

**Parent:** LIN-4195 "Costs rebuild 2: one record per model request, summed". Its full design (decisions D1–D14, the replay change list, the witnesses, the order of landing) is in LIN-4195's description under "## Implementation Plan". The plan-review notes are in LIN-4195's comment `eedab867-0fe0-4b15-b74a-2b78240f11d1`. The numbered notes cited here ("review note N") refer to that comment.

Session fit: fits one session
Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4195's approving plan-review (comment eedab867-0fe0-4b15-b74a-2b78240f11d1, rev 1)
Grounding commits: Harbour (JKershaw/LinearViewer) `72305215`, runner (JKershaw/simple-dispatcher) `cc2650a`. At breakdown (2026-11-04 \~01:45Z) neither repo had a commit after these.

The parent's approved plan is this piece's starting point; read it in full in LIN-4195's description. Follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so on LIN-4195.

## Implemented (close-out, 2026-11-04)

Merged as PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2273](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2273>), squashed as `2ee4e600`, deployed 16:36Z. The work follows the survey's recommended shape and the 11:15Z scope decision, with one deviation: scope item 2 (loading becomes part of the read) was split into LIN-4226, as the scope decision allows and as recorded on LIN-4195. The production gate passed GO before the merge (comment `3038e924`). The close-out summary is comment `3dbbe64c`. The pre-work survey's design guidance (its recommended shape and at-merge checks) is pruned from here. The full history is in the task snapshots (2026-11-04T16:39Z) and the comment trail.

**Not this task's** (list them in the close-out, don't file them):

* retiring the snapshot fold once no snapshot-only lineage is left in the window;
* callers passing a cost source once;
* splitting `readCalls`/`callsSurfaceOf` out of `cost-read.js`;
* how instance-wide reads meet stores keyed by workspace;
* whether stored run paragraphs keep pre-cutover figures.

The label change remains John's call (named in the description).

## Added at LIN-4200 close-out: gate conditions carried into this piece's acceptance

Piece 3 (LIN-4200, merged as `230cc2c2`) measured live data and recorded a NO-GO for this piece as things stand (LIN-4195 comment `0beba2a2-4378-4ee6-a46a-d5f1291b59ec`). These conditions are added to the acceptance above.

* **Blocked by LIN-4212** (wake rows strand request records under their own id; `listForAnchors` would drop them). Acceptance there: zero orphan records when re-measured.
* **Workspace KPIs read (D13):** the records-sum path adds about 1.2 s at the steady 30-day volume (about 230k records), on top of 0.83 s today. Before the read switch, put it behind the same stale-while-revalidate cache that `/kpis` uses (`lib/kpi-page.js`, 60 s), or build the D13 pre-sum fallback. `/kpis` itself needs no fallback. The pre-sum fallback has not been timed. Evidence: LIN-4200 beat-3 comment, `scripts/lin-4200-d13-volume-timing.mjs`.
* **Re-measure before the switch:** the to-the-cent subset was empty after the ruling `lin4200-to-cent-rule` (7 eligible, all true same-walk races, 0 agreements), so there is no agreement evidence yet. Re-run `scripts/lin-4200-measure-records-vs-snapshots.mjs` once enough clean lineages exist, and require agreement at the token level and to the cent.

### From the Periodicals (top-down, 4 Nov), in this task's ground

The 4 Nov Drift & Coherence and Seams & Tangles reviews found these in the area this piece rewires. Neither review handed them to a ticket. They're listed here so this task can carry what it cheaply can, and **name in the close-out** what it doesn't.

* `lineage-identity-read-twins` (Drift #11): `lib/founder-lookup.js:34-61` repeats `dispatch-store.js:1953-1975`'s query, and the copy skips the bounded-read guard and fault mapping. It came from LIN-4178. The one loader is the natural single home.
* `usage-record-vocabulary-two-readers` (Drift #10, "hand to LIN-4201"): `lane` is a closed set in the snapshot reader (`session-telemetry.js:398`) but open in the record intake (`request-usage-intake.js:41,68-76`); the token-field list exists three times per repo plus the kit. The records-first read should name one vocabulary.
* `cost-fold-partition-restated` (Drift #18): `cost-read.js:63-86` restates `row-usage.js:71-77`'s snapshot/delta partition. The one decision function this piece adds is its home.
* **The cost read is a hub in the catch-all** (Seams N1/N6): 9 cross-area importers from 5 areas, reaching both ways into Runs and LLM. Seams is "watching, not ticketing" because of this piece. The at-merge check above (a home in `areas.json`) is the answer it's waiting for. Note that a home on the map doesn't remove the two-way reach. Say in the close-out whether the loader removes any of it.

### Scope decision (4 Nov, 11:15 UTC)

John asked Claude to take the human's role in this process and choose a large enough option. **The decision is the larger version of the recommended shape.** Everything below is part of this ticket's Done, not optional:

1. **One loader and one decision**, as above. Since LIN-4212 merged (`eb44eff9`), the loader reads records by their posting row (member rows), not the wake's stamp.
2. **Loading becomes part of the read.** The seven callers have to be touched anyway, so each passes a cost source (the loader) to the read once, instead of loading for itself. The next input to the read should then touch no caller. *(This was the step-back's "right direction, not this task's"; it's pulled in because this task already pays for the seven caller edits.)*
3. **Remove the routed copies, don't just name them:** `lib/founder-lookup.js` goes, with its query served by the one loader or by the store method it repeats, keeping the bounded-read guard; `cost-read.js:63-86` stops restating `row-usage`'s partition; and records and snapshots share one named `lane` and token-field vocabulary.
4. **A home on the map:** `cost-read`, `row-usage` and the loader go into a real area in `scripts/code-shape/areas.json`. Say in the close-out whether the loader removed any of the hub's two-way reach into Runs and LLM.

**Proving still comes first** (the replay serving records, the expected diff as a failing test). Split into pieces if that's needed to prove each one; say so on LIN-4195. Not in scope: retiring the snapshot fold (it's still needed for pre-deploy lineages in the window).

comments.body:
**Note from LIN-4197 review (piece 0, now merged): two requirements for piece 4's harness and baseline.**

Harbour PR #2264 (merged as `1b6c675`) added a mixed-harness control to `tests/fixtures/cost-replay/`. Two things piece 4 must do for it to mean anything:
1. **Wire `requestRecords` into the replay's store.** The control "removing them leaves the replay unchanged" passes by construction today, because nothing in `tests/fixtures/cost-replay/harness.js` reads `requestRecords`. Piece 4 must feed the records into the replay so that this assertion flips for a real reason, and then make the lineage choice (opencode delta rows plus claude-code records; today mh-haiku is withheld as a whole lineage and its $0.25 opencode delta disappears, oracle $0.2755) deliberately.
2. **Diff against `goldens-lin4197.json`, not `goldens.json`.** `goldens.json` is deliberately left at the LIN-4177 baseline, paired with `expected-changes.json` (W9 diffs HEAD against it). The piece-0 HEAD baseline is `tests/fixtures/cost-replay/goldens-lin4197.json`. Do not run `scripts/cost-replay.mjs --record` without re-baselining the change list: it rewrites `goldens.json`.

## Note from LIN-4202 close-out

Piece 5 merged (Harbour `5334c81a`, runner `765289d4`). One acceptance item of LIN-4202 is carried here because it can only run once this piece lands: if you choose **per-harness scoping**, confirm one opencode lineage with records reads its cost from records and that cost equals its snapshot sum; if you choose the **mixed-harness control**, confirm no live lineage mixes `harness` values across its `request-usage` documents. opencode now posts `harness:'opencode'` records (when `SD_WORKER_USAGE_RELAY` is on), so opencode lineages will have records once an operator's runner runs the new code.

## Gate pass criterion for this ticket (ruled by John, 2026-11-04 09:49Z)

Decision `lin4201-gate-pass-criterion`, answered verbatim: **"GO when the re-measure shows 0 orphan records and every difference explained to the token (race, late reap post, or pricing), even with an empty cent subset. Cost: no direct cent-agreement sample; relies on token-exact explanation."**

What this means for piece 4:
- Precondition: LIN-4212 (orphan-anchor fix) lands first.
- Then re-run `scripts/lin-4200-measure-records-vs-snapshots.mjs` read-only against production. GO requires: **0 orphan records** in the window, and **every** records-vs-snapshot difference explained to the token as one of: same-walk race, late reap-flush post, or per-request vs last-model pricing. An empty to-the-cent subset no longer blocks.
- Carried conditions from LIN-4200 still apply: workspace-KPIs needs caching or the D13 pre-sum fallback before shipping; the read must sum records regardless of post time (late reap posts included).

Context: LIN-4195 comment `0beba2a2` (NO-GO report), LIN-4212.

**LIN-4201: note on "by anchor" in `listForAnchors` (from LIN-4212, PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2272).** "By anchor" now means the posting row's current anchor, not the stamp stored at post time. `RequestUsageStore.listForAnchors(urlKey, anchors)` resolves the member rows itself from `dispatch-history` (`rootItemId` in anchors, no status or `isMember` filter), reads records by `itemId`, relabels each record to its row's current anchor, drops records whose `itemId` has no member row, and folds to one record per `requestId`. The signature, callers, the required `historyCollection` argument and review note 3 are unchanged. The LIN-4200 measure script now calls this loader. A pre-sum fallback must not group by the stored stamp. The loader also returns `itemId` and `updatedAt`.

LIN-4212 (the blocker for this piece) is merged and deployed: PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2272, `eb44eff`, deployment `success` 2026-11-04T11:12Z. Before this piece's read switch, an operator still needs to run three production checks (not run by the LIN-4212 close-out, no credential): the live re-measure (`orphanRecords == 0`, `duplicateAfterRead == 0`, the three `88f03588…` records reachable), the `{urlKey, itemId}` index check with IXSCAN, and the `lin-4200-d13-volume-timing.mjs` re-time. Details are in the LIN-4212 "Close-out" comment.

## LIN-4201: PR open, CI green

**PR:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2273
**Head commit:** `3780cb0694149b9c10a0cdab7474b95acf646b19`. Beats: `923f0fde` record fold, `63cc74d6` cutover and required `requestRows`, `67293d76` census, replay and cache, `faca8b7d` code-shape map, `3780cb06` CI fix.
**CI:** green on `3780cb06`, run https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/41831795810: Unit tests, E2E shards 1-4, Secret scan and CI success all passed.
- The first run (on `faca8b7d`, https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/actions/runs/41830363924) failed on Unit tests. `tests/unit/mongo-smoke.test.js` runs only against a real mongod, so local runs skipped it, and it called `collectKpiStats` without `requestRows`. That is the required-argument throw catching a missed caller.
- Fixed in `3780cb06`. Both CI unit arms were then mirrored locally with a real mongod: 23,149 pass, 0 fail each.
**Local runs** (without mongod, at `faca8b7d`):
- `test:unit` 23,076 / 0 fail
- `test:hermetic` 23,076 / 0 fail, zero non-loopback sockets
- `test:clock-shift` 23,076 / 0 fail
- `secret-scan` pass
- 10 cost-page Playwright specs: 115 passed

The task stays In Progress. Merge and Done wait for review.

### What it does
- **One decision** (`lib/cost-read.js` `lineageUsageOf`): a lineage with request records reads them (`foldRequestUsage`); one without reads its snapshots exactly as before.
- **Per-harness scoping:** a snapshot of a harness that has no records still counts. That only happens in the window before piece 5; the runner never mixes harnesses.
- **The mixed-harness control is asserted directly:** `mh-haiku` = $0.2755 (its oracle), and `mh-sonnet` does not move.
- **`requestRows` is required** by `readCost`, `lineageRecords`, `lineageFigureOf` and `buildRunView`; each throws without it.
- **The one loader** (`lib/request-usage-loader.js`, over `listForAnchors`) is injected into every caller.
- **`buildSessionTelemetry` is left in place.** It does not read usage (since LIN-4136), and its caller uses runtime, metrics and model.
- **Reader census:**
  - `harnessReadingOf` is now records-aware: a record lineage has a known harness and is not delta-summed.
  - The snapshot/delta partition is stated once (`countedRowsOf`).
  - Kept, as legacy-fold-only: `model-pricing.js:421`, `kpiUsageEntry`, `kpi-stats.js:460`.
  - A census test fails on any new reader.

### Replay (baseline `goldens-lin4197.json` only)
- **Before:** with records withheld, the replay equals the golden exactly. The one addition to the golden is the records-only section (e), recorded at `eb44eff9`.
- **After:** with records read, the diff equals `lin4201-change-list.json` exactly, both ways.
- **Items:** (a) 84 paths, (b) 37, (c) 18, (d) 37, (e) 48. (f) has no diff by design; it equals its oracle, counted once.
- **Controls unchanged:** the existing corpus, S2/S3/S4/S7, the five single-model stages (to 1e-9), and `mh-sonnet`.
- **For John (review note 10):** the (b) label change, claude-haiku-5-5 → claude-opus-5, moves mixed-model lineages between groups on Models and in the effort read-out.

### Rulings recorded
- **Workspace KPIs: the cache is kept** (an in-ticket engineering choice; LIN-4200's carried condition allows the cache or the pre-sum).
  - Measured on a local mongod at steady-state volume (231k records): fetch 1.18 s plus fold 0.17 s, about +1.35 s per load.
  - The page is now served from a per-workspace stale-while-revalidate cache (60 s, as `/kpis`). No pre-sum was built.
  - **Behaviour change for review:** the workspace KPIs page and its weekly-budget cost series can be up to 60 s stale.
  - The timing run also found and fixed a call-stack overflow in the loader at that volume.
- **Live measurements were not run.** There is no production credential here, and the Railway root credential flagged on LIN-4195 for rotation was deliberately not read.

### Code-shape map and hub reach
- `cost-read`, `row-usage`, `lineage-membership` and `founder-lookup` move into Runs & dispatch, beside `request-usage-*`. `workspace-kpis-cache` goes to Reports.
- **Does the loader remove any of the hub's two-way reach into Runs/LLM? No.**
  - `seams.mjs` at `eb44eff9` and at `67293d76`, with the same guide: the Runs ⇄ LLM knot goes from 29/36 to 30/37 crossings.
  - Added: `model-routing-history → request-usage-loader` and `request-usage-fold → model-pricing`. Removed: none.

### Post-deploy items NOT run
Each needs a read-only production URI. John or an operator can run them.
1. `scripts/lin-4200-d13-volume-timing.mjs` (live timing; the collectors now include the records load).
2. `scripts/lin-4200-measure-records-vs-snapshots.mjs`. The gate (`lin4201-gate-pass-criterion`) requires `orphanRecords == 0`, `duplicateAfterRead == 0`, the three `88f03588…` records reachable, and every difference explained to the token.
3. The `{urlKey, itemId}` IXSCAN check on `request-usage` (from LIN-4212).
4. The live priced share after deploy, per piece 3's method. **Not recorded.**
5. The LIN-4202 carry-over: an opencode lineage with records reads its cost from records, and that equals its snapshot sum.

**Not done in this PR (scope decision item 3):** removing `lib/founder-lookup.js` and sharing one `lane`/token-field vocabulary. Listed, not filed.

## Autopilot (stepper) run summary — implementation step

Ran LIN-4201's implementation as 4 beats in one warm session (worker session 742ee005, ROOT dispatch `1e599b49-49cb-4522-9021-67b5b5f4531f`).

| Beat | Dispatch | Result (verified from the worker's report) |
|---|---|---|
| 1/4 pure `foldRequestUsage` | 1e599b49 | `923f0fde`; 20 tests, 16/20 red on stub, 8 mutations caught; unit suite green |
| 2/4 records-first decision + required `requestRows` | 7486666e | `63cc74d6`; 8 production call sites + loader; 27/34 red on beat-1 code, per-caller reverts caught; unit/hermetic 23,036 / 0 fail |
| 3/4 reader census, replay, timing | 15cf58dc | `67293d76`; replay diff equals the change list exactly vs `goldens-lin4197.json`; 23,075 / 0 fail |
| 4/4 code-shape map, PR, CI | 3a40e708 | PR #2273, head `3780cb06`; first CI run red (missed caller in `tests/unit/mongo-smoke.test.js`, caught by the required-arg throw), fixed |

**Evidence (checked by me):** PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2273 is OPEN against main, mergeable, head `3780cb06`; all 7 checks (Unit tests, E2E 1-4, Secret scan, CI success) COMPLETED/SUCCESS on that commit. Not merged; task stays In Progress.

**Rulings by the orchestrator (in-ticket engineering choices):** workspace-KPIs keeps the 60 s stale-while-revalidate cache rather than the D13 pre-sum (the ticket's carried condition allows either). The up-to-60 s staleness on the workspace KPIs page / weekly budget is a behaviour change for review to weigh. Per-harness scoping stands (the ticket's accepted direction); the mixed-harness control is asserted directly. `buildSessionTelemetry` left in place (it never reads usage).

**For review to look at:**
- Code-shape map: the loader did NOT remove any of the cost hub's two-way reach into Runs/LLM; the Runs <-> LLM tangle went 29/36 -> 30/37 crossings (added `model-routing-history -> request-usage-loader`, `request-usage-fold -> model-pricing`; removed none).
- `goldens-lin4197.json` gained one case (e, records-only); every existing section is byte-identical.
- Existing tests were edited for plumbing only (wrappers/renames) plus one shape pin (`readModelsHistory` empty result gains `requestRows: []`) and the store-census `ALLOWED` entry.

**Post-deploy items NOT run (need a read-only production URI; operator):** live timing (`scripts/lin-4200-d13-volume-timing.mjs`), live re-measure vs the gate (`scripts/lin-4200-measure-records-vs-snapshots.mjs`), the `{urlKey, itemId}` IXSCAN check from LIN-4212, the live priced share (piece 3's method), the LIN-4202 opencode check. The mixed-model label change (haiku -> opus) is John's call per review note 10. Not in this PR: removing `lib/founder-lookup.js` and sharing the lane/token-field vocabulary (scope item 3).

Next: independent `review` of PR #2273, then `close-out` if approved.

## Review — LIN-4201

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2273 at head `3780cb0694149b9c10a0cdab7474b95acf646b19`, base `eb44eff9`. Main has not moved since then.

CI: green on `3780cb06` (Unit tests, E2E 1–4, Secret scan, CI success, all SUCCESS). The PR is mergeable.

### What holds up (checked myself)
- **The one decision.** `lib/cost-read.js` `lineageUsageOf` makes the records-vs-snapshots choice in one place, scoped per harness, with a null harness read as claude-code. `foldRequestUsage` (`lib/request-usage-fold.js`) is pure. Native `costUsd` wins. The labels and completeness follow D6. Review note 3 is stated in code and tested.
- **The required argument.** `readCost`, `lineageRecords`, `lineageFigureOf` and `buildRunView` throw without `requestRows`. Every production caller is wired to the one loader: `/cost`, Models (settings and dispatch), effort read-out, `/kpis`, workspace KPIs, the run page and the run-paragraph hook. No caller imports `RequestUsageStore`. The only `[]` passes are deliberate, in two scripts: the measure script's snapshot side and `lin3014/capture-kpis.mjs`.
- **Partition.** It is stated once (`countedRowsOf`). The census is broadened. `buildSessionTelemetry` is kept, with the reason given. The code-shape map is updated.
- **Mutation checks.** I ran each against 6 LIN-4201 test files (121 tests), and every one went red. All were reverted and the tree is clean.
  - Counting same-harness snapshots beside records fails (f), the "counted once" test and "every path the change list names still differs". This is the ticket's own mutation.
  - Removing the required-arg throw fails the "throws without requestRows" tests.
  - Ignoring records entirely fails the replay flip and the `/cost` route test.
  - Dropping per-harness scoping fails the opencode-delta-beside-records test.
  - Removing the native-`costUsd` win fails the `/cost` and Models route tests (`unpriced`).
  - Labelling by latest instead of cost-dominant fails the labels test and "no path differs that the change list does not name".
- **Regression check.** The cost files' history (LIN-4129…4179, 4212) shows no reverted or re-applied change.

### Gaps against the plan
The 11:15Z scope decision says items 1–4 are "part of this ticket's Done, not optional". The only allowed alternative is to split, and say so on LIN-4195.
- **Item 2 (loading becomes part of the read): not done, and not mentioned in the PR or the comments.** Each of the seven callers still loads for itself (`loader.forAnchors`/`forRows`) and passes `requestRows`. The read never takes a cost source. So the next input to the read will touch every caller again, which is the exact thing item 2 was pulled in to prevent.
- **Item 3, partly not done.** `lib/founder-lookup.js` still exists; the PR moved it on the area map rather than removing it. The token-field vocabulary is still restated: `row-usage.js:29` `TOKEN_FIELDS`, `request-usage-store.js:54` `USAGE_TOKEN_FIELDS`, `runner-kit/runner.mjs:596`, and the measure script. `lane` is still open in intake and closed in the snapshot reader. The PR says "Listed, not filed". Under LIN-2825 neither listing nor filing discharges scope.
- **Review note 10 on LIN-4195: not done.** The (b) label change (claude-haiku-5-5 → claude-opus-5) is named in the PR but not on LIN-4195. There is no LIN-4195 comment after 08:46Z.

- **LIN-4212**: already Done.
- **LIN-4195**: the label change (review note 10) is still John's call. It is not a merge gate.

### Operator housekeeping (no secrets)
The Railway SSH key `lin4200-measurement` (`~/.ssh/id_ed25519_railway_lin4200`) is still registered; I used it and left it in place. Remove it when it is no longer wanted. No credential was printed in this session.

## Survey 1a (round 3)

My part was the revision after review: scope item 3, the split of item 2, and the note-10 comment. The first pass was earlier beats.

**1. Why was this difficult?** The logic wasn't hard; the breadth was. Removing `founder-lookup.js` meant changing one query, but it was reached through an injected function. Tests pinned `server.js` source text, the replay harness used it, and two scripts imported it. The store census also flagged my new vocabulary module, because its doc comment named the store file. Item 2 bound harder. `/kpis` loads records once, instance-wide, through `forRows`, and the read is synchronous. Loading inside the read means an async read across nine callers without losing that batching. That is a redesign, not an edit.

**2. What would I have done first?** Grep every caller of the read and the loader, and the census regexes, before deciding anything. That count is what made the split obvious. I reached it after reading half the files.

**3. What would I tidy?** The runner kit still has its own token-field list, pinned by a test rather than shared. `dispatch-store.js` now has two entry shapes for one query: the method and the raw-collection function the KPI path needs. The tests that regex-match `server.js` wiring are brittle and should exercise the wiring instead. The store method's switch to string-`_id` dedupe is harmless but deserves a direct test.

**4. If the area were how I'd want it, what would the ticket have been?** "Add request records to the cost source." The read would already take a source, so this would be one loader file and the fold, with no caller edits and no required-argument plumbing.

**5. What did the ticket get wrong?** It priced item 2 as nearly free, on the grounds that "the seven callers have to be touched anyway". Touching a caller to pass an array is not the same change as making the read async and moving batching into it. It also put a production re-measure in an implementation ticket's acceptance. The implementer can't hold that credential, so the task was certain to end with the gate open.

**6. What did the change leave behind?** Simpler: one lineage-identity query with its guard, and one token-field and lane list. New: `request-usage-vocabulary.js`, which has a home because the `request-usage-*` area pattern already covers it. Still in two places: the runner kit's field list, and the method-vs-function shapes of the identity read. Open: LIN-4226 (item 2).

**7. Did the larger scope pay for itself?** Partly.
- **Item 3 paid:** about 20 files, mostly mechanical. It removed a copy that skipped the bounded-read guard, real drift caught cheaply.
- **Item 4 (map placement)** landed in the first pass as asked.
- **Item 2 didn't land.** Its cost was a full review round trip spent finding that out, then a split. Asked as a separate piece from the start, it would have cost the same work with one fewer review.

The larger scope was right to name item 3 and wrong to assume item 2 rode along.
